written.q: Explain the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot, and describe the agent loop.
written.a: A chatbot replies with text. An AI agent receives a goal, interprets instructions, may call tools and may coordinate with other agents to complete a task. The agent loop: sense the environment (percepts or user goal), decide, act through tools/actuators, observe the result and repeat.

written.q: Describe the n8n lecture hall booking workflow for both outcomes.
written.a: Form trigger (requester name, email, date, start and end time) → Edit Fields builds startDateTime / endDateTime in Asia/Colombo → Google Calendar checks the slot → IF available: create a Calendar event with the booking details, a Basic LLM Chain with a Gemini Chat Model writes a short confirmation email, Gmail sends it, Form Ending shows success; if unavailable: Form Ending shows an unavailable message.

written.q: Explain root agent, sub-agent, tool, session and event in Google ADK.
written.a: Root agent: main entry point and coordinator that routes to one child without doing specialist work. Sub-agent: a specialist child (intake, billing, outage...). Tool: a controlled deterministic capability (Python function) registered on the agent that owns it. Session: one conversation, new one per test. Events: trace of which agent ran, transfers, tool calls with input and output, and errors.

written.q: Compare SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent and LoopAgent with a use for each.
written.a: All are deterministic workflow agents. Sequential runs children in order (understand request → classify → retrieve record → explain). Parallel runs independent children concurrently (outage and bill lookup). Loop repeats a child workflow until a stop condition or maximum iterations (use a small maximum to avoid infinite loops).

written.q: What should the language model do and what should tools do? Give a safe flow for writing a record.
written.a: Model: understand requests, decide intent, ask concise follow-ups, explain structured results. Tools: read files, apply exact rules, check duplicates, allocate identifiers, append validated rows; never let the LLM invent stored values. Safe write: present proposed data, obtain explicit choice, check for duplicate, validate again, perform one write, report the tool's result.

written.q: List what a good LLM-agent instruction should state.
written.a: Its responsibility; the information it needs; the information it must not request or handle; the tools it owns; what to do when information is missing; the expected response style; its authority and side-effect boundaries.
